title: 2nd Sitting of second session of 2026
summary: The Majlis swore in Abdulla Sodig, who won the North Hithadhoo by-election, announced a committee seat change, and sent several presidential nominations to committees. Members debated the government's Cyber Security Bill, which was accepted 66-0 and sent to the Information and Communication Technology Committee. Debate on the Personal Data Protection Bill began but was put off to another day. The Majlis then approved ambassador nominations for the UAE (57-10) and Qatar (57-9).

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Thanked the sponsor of the Personal Data Protection Bill but questioned who will enforce it, citing alleged misuse of Vaikaradhoo residents' data.
Asked why ministers are removed and later posted abroad, and said he could not back the ambassador nominations without an explanation.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Welcomed the new North Hithadhoo member and spoke about his party before the chair asked him to return to the bill.
Said the law is important but needs capacity, experts and infrastructure to work; proposed changes at committee stage.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Congratulated the new member and supported the Cyber Security Bill, urging independent institutions staffed by trustworthy people.
On the Personal Data Protection Bill, asked how data held in the Majlis is protected and called for strong rules and penalties.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the Cyber Security Bill gives wide powers to one security body, personal data safeguards are weak, and the Majlis role needs defining.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the bill, citing cyber-attacks on businesses and the lack of a law to punish offenders; said personal data is released only by court order.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill as important, said people already trust banks with their data, and urged committee work and highlighting its benefits.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Called it a good bill but wanted businesses and legal experts consulted and penalties against misuse of data, including by government bodies.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Backed the bill, saying cyber security is now a basic need, and listed protection of personal data, protection from ransomware and action against offenders.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the bill fits the President's plan for round-the-clock digital government alongside the Digital Transformation and Digital Identity bills, and supported it.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report: it passed unanimously on 11 June, finding the UAE and Qatar nominees suitable and recommending approval.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the report, saying both nominees are capable and ambassadors can help bring economic projects and links with Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 15 to 20 of the first session of 2026 were accepted without amendment.
Husnee Mubarik (Manadhoo) replaces Ibrahim Falah (Inguraidhoo) on the Housing committee for the PNC.
Abdulla Sodig was sworn in as member for North Hithadhoo.
Non-resident ambassador nominations were referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The reallocation of ministry work areas and the Finance Minister nomination were referred to the Government Oversight Committee.
The Elections Commission nomination was referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The retirement-benefits motion for former police and military personnel was withdrawn by its sponsor.
The Cyber Security Bill was accepted and sent to the Information and Communication Technology Committee.
Debate on the Personal Data Protection Bill was put off to another day.
The Majlis approved Tariq Ibrahim as ambassador to the UAE and Adam Shareef Umar as ambassador to Qatar.
The next sitting was set for 17 June 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Cyber Security Bill (sponsor: Hussain Nasih, Central Henveyru)
Approve Tariq Ibrahim as ambassador to the United Arab Emirates
Approve Adam Shareef Umar as ambassador to the State of Qatar
